skill.name: p2p-networking
skill.description: Guides Rust peer-to-peer networking patterns for decentralized code collaboration using commonware concepts.
skill.summary: Rust-focused P2P networking guidance for message design, peer management, gossip, repository sync, and secure configuration.

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, code fences, and Rust protocol examples. The audit confirms one network exposure risk from binding to 0.0.0.0 and one semantic concern where gossip data is processed before validation is shown.

remediation.issue: Default listener binds to all interfaces.
remediation.suggestion: Use 127.0.0.1 for local examples, or clearly warn users before binding production nodes to 0.0.0.0.

remediation.issue: Gossip handler omits validation before processing peer data.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit size, schema, topic, signature, and rate checks before process_message and rebroadcast steps.

content.value_statement: Decentralized code collaboration needs clear peer communication patterns. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code draft Rust P2P designs with commonware concepts.
actual_capabilities: Explains a Rust message enum for peer handshakes, repository sync, gossip, and keep-alive traffic.
Shows peer manager structure with connection setup, peer state, and broadcast flow.
Outlines gossip deduplication, fanout selection, message processing, and rebroadcast behavior.
Describes repository synchronization through refs, missing object detection, fetching, and local storage.
Defines network configuration fields for listen address, bootstrap nodes, limits, timeouts, and keypairs.
Lists security considerations for authentication, encryption, rate limiting, peer scoring, and validation.
limitations: Examples are Rust-oriented and depend on types that are not fully defined in the skill.
The skill does not provide a complete runnable P2P node implementation.
Bootstrap discovery, DHT behavior, and NAT traversal are only described at a high level.
Production hardening requires additional validation, monitoring, abuse controls, and deployment review.

use_cases.title: Design a P2P Protocol
use_cases.description: Plan message types, handshake flow, gossip topics, and repository sync behavior for a decentralized collaboration tool.

use_cases.title: Draft Rust Networking Components
use_cases.description: Use the examples as structure for peer managers, connection state, broadcast paths, and configuration models.

use_cases.title: Review Network Security Requirements
use_cases.description: Identify authentication, encryption, rate limiting, validation, and peer scoring controls needed before production use.

prompt_templates.title: Harden Gossip Handling

output_examples.input: Explain the role of the peer manager.
output_examples.output: A peer manager tracks connected peers, stores their capabilities, opens authenticated connections, and broadcasts messages across active connections.

output_examples.input: Review my gossip protocol for safety.
output: Validate message size and topic before processing.
Apply per-peer rate limits and update peer scores after abuse.

output_examples.output: The sync flow should discover peers with the repository, compare refs, request missing objects, verify objects, and store validated data locally.

best_practices: Treat the snippets as architecture guidance and add production checks before deployment.
Use explicit validation for every message received from a peer.
Document network binding, bootstrap node, key management, and rate limit choices.
anti_patterns: Binding public listeners by default without an operator warning.
Processing gossip payloads before validation and abuse checks.
Copying sample types directly without defining trust boundaries and failure behavior.

faq.question: What programming language does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Rust and uses commonware-style P2P networking concepts.

faq.question: Does this skill create a complete P2P node?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and examples that need integration, testing, and hardening.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What security topics does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers authentication, encryption, rate limiting, peer scoring, and message validation at a planning level.

faq.question: Is the default network address production ready?
faq.answer: No. Review any 0.0.0.0 listener before deployment because it exposes the service on all interfaces.

faq.question: What should I add before using the examples?
faq.answer: Add complete validation, error handling, tests, abuse controls, observability, and deployment-specific configuration.
